How Deep Can a Leatherback Turtle Dive?.caption:
How Deep Can a Leatherback Turtle Dive? 🐢

Leatherbacks, the giant sea turtles of the open ocean, are record-breaking divers. Tracking tags have recorded leatherbacks diving more than 1,200 meters (over 4,000 feet), the deepest dive ever recorded for a turtle. They go that deep to hunt jellyfish.

How Slow Can a Blue Whale's Heart Beat?.caption:
How Slow Can a Blue Whale's Heart Beat? 🐋

In 2019, scientists tagged a wild blue whale off California and recorded its heartbeat for the first time. During deep feeding dives its heart usually beat just 4 to 8 times a minute, and sometimes only 2 times a minute. Back at the surface, it sped up to 25 to 37 beats a minute.

Do Killer Whales Go Through Menopause? 🐋.caption:
Do Killer Whales Go Through Menopause? 🐋

Female killer whales are one of the very few animals, like humans, that go through menopause. They stop having babies in their 30s or 40s, but can live into their 90s. Those grandmothers stay with their families and help them survive.

How Big Are a Giant Squid's Eyes? 🦑

Giant squid have the largest eyes of any animal on Earth. Each eye can grow to about 10 inches across, roughly the size of a dinner plate. That is nearly three times wider than the eyes of any other living animal.

How Many Eyes Does a Box Jellyfish Have?.caption:
How Many Eyes Does a Box Jellyfish Have? 🪼

A box jellyfish has 24 eyes, grouped into four clusters of six. In each cluster, four simple eyes sense light and dark, while two have lenses that can form images. The upper lens eyes always point upward, no matter how the jellyfish turns.

What Is the Loudest Animal on Earth? 🐋

The sperm whale makes the loudest sound ever measured from an animal. Its clicks can reach up to 236 decibels underwater, and each click lasts only about 100 microseconds. The whale uses these powerful clicks as long-range sonar in the deep sea.

Spinner dolphins are some of the most acrobatic dolphins in the ocean. They leap out of the water and can spin up to seven times in the air before splashing back down. Scientists think the spins may help them communicate or shake off hitchhiking remoras.

The giant Pacific octopus is the biggest octopus in the world, and its eight arms are lined with suckers. Each arm can have up to 280 suckers, which adds up to more than 2,000 in all. The octopus uses them to grip, hold food and feel its way around.

How Long Can a Sea Turtle Sleep Underwater? 🐢

Sea turtles breathe air, but they can sleep underwater on one breath. While foraging they usually dive for about 20 to 40 minutes, but when sleeping they can stay down for several hours. The longest stays, up to about seven hours, happen in cold winter water.

How Much Does an Elephant Seal Sleep at Sea? 🦭

During months at sea, northern elephant seals sleep only about two hours a day. They nap during deep dives, often around ten minutes at a time, and in REM sleep they roll upside down and drift down in a 'sleep spiral.' Back on the beach, they can sleep up to about ten hours a day.

Lots of people believe peeing on a jellyfish sting makes it feel better. But scientists have tested it, and pee does not help. It can even push the tiny stingers left on your skin to release more venom, so rinse with seawater and ask a lifeguard for help instead.

How Long Can a Sperm Whale Hold Its Brea.caption:
How Long Can a Sperm Whale Hold Its Breath? 🐋

When a sperm whale dives deep to hunt for food, one dive can last about 45 minutes on a single breath. Some dives last even longer. Afterward, it rests at the surface for several minutes to breathe before diving again.
